questions.title: ACID Letters
questions.description: In the ACID guarantees, the D stands for…

questions.title: Commit Meaning
questions.description: What does COMMIT do to the work performed since BEGIN?
questions.Option3: Makes it permanent, visible to later readers

questions.title: Rollback Effect
questions.description: After BEGIN, one UPDATE ran, then ROLLBACK. What does the data look like?
questions.Option2: Exactly as it was before BEGIN

questions.title: Default Autocommit
questions.description: Outside an explicit transaction in SQLite, each standalone statement is…
questions.Option4: Its own implicit transaction, committed immediately

questions.title: SAVEPOINT Purpose
questions.description: Why does a transaction create a SAVEPOINT?
questions.Option3: To undo part of the transaction without discarding all of it

questions.title: Transfer With Rollback
questions.description: Account id 1 starts at 250000. What does the snippet's SELECT print?

questions.title: RELEASE Savepoint
questions.description: What does RELEASE s1 do to the work done after SAVEPOINT s1?
questions.Option1: Undoes it back to the savepoint
questions.Option4: Merges it upward and removes the savepoint (committing only if s1 was the outermost savepoint)

questions.title: Visibility of Uncommitted Work
questions.description: Connection A runs the snippet (no COMMIT yet). When can connection B first read the +1 change?
questions.Option1: While the transaction is still open
questions.codesnippet:
BEGIN;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 1 WHERE id = 3;

questions.title: Atomicity Meaning
questions.description: The A in ACID promises that…
questions.Option2: All statements in the transaction apply, or none do

questions.title: Ending a Transaction
questions.description: Which pair of statements both END a transaction?

questions.title: SQLite Isolation Default
questions.description: With its default journaling, SQLite gives concurrent connections…
questions.Option1: Dirty reads of uncommitted data by default
questions.Option3: Serializable behavior — writers and readers never see partial transactions
questions.Option4: Full multi-version snapshot isolation with MVCC

questions.title: ROLLBACK TO Semantics
questions.description: Account id 4 starts at 500000. What does the snippet's SELECT print, and why?
questions.Option1: 500000 — undone, and the transaction is still open
questions.Option4: An error — ROLLBACK TO requires an explicit BEGIN first

questions.title: BEGIN IMMEDIATE
questions.description: How does BEGIN IMMEDIATE differ from a plain BEGIN in SQLite?
questions.Option1: It commits instantly after each statement
questions.Option2: It is invalid without WAL mode
questions.Option4: It acquires the write (RESERVED) lock at BEGIN, not at the first write

questions.title: Deadlock Recipe
questions.description: A classic deadlock between two sessions needs…
questions.Option1: One transaction and one idle reader
questions.Option2: Two sessions each holding a lock the other needs, acquired in opposite order
questions.Option3: A missing index on the join column
questions.Option4: Too many savepoints in one transaction

questions.title: Deadlock Prevention
questions.description: The most effective habit for preventing deadlocks is…
questions.Option1: Touching rows and tables in a consistent order and keeping transactions short
questions.Option3: Making transactions longer to hold locks safely

questions.title: Savepoint Ladder Outcome
questions.description: Account id 1 starts at 100000. What does the snippet's final SELECT print?
questions.Option3: 100000 — both updates happened after s1 and were rolled back

questions.title: Lock Ladder
questions.description: Which is the correct escalation of SQLite's classic (rollback-journal) lock states?
questions.Option4: SQLite takes no locks at all

questions.title: Durability Mechanism
questions.description: What makes a committed SQLite transaction survive a crash (the D in ACID)?
questions.Option1: An in-memory copy of the database
questions.Option2: The operating system file cache alone
questions.Option4: The rollback journal or WAL, synced to disk before COMMIT returns

questions.title: Nested Savepoint Chain
questions.description: The table t starts with v = 0. What does v hold after the snippet completes?
questions.Option3: 1 — only the b-savepoint work was undone (RELEASE a then ends the transaction)

questions.title: Isolation Levels Order
questions.description: Ordered weakest to strongest, the standard SQL isolation levels are…
questions.Option1: READ UNCOMMITTED -> READ COMMITTED -> REPEATABLE READ -> SERIALIZABLE
questions.Option2: SERIALIZABLE -> REPEATABLE READ -> READ COMMITTED -> READ UNCOMMITTED
questions.Option3: They are unordered — any one may be chosen freely
questions.Option4: SQLite implements all four simultaneously with MVCC
